text:
Samir Hassan: Need help reconciling a messy airfare booking. Booked refundable ticket for client trip via TravelHub on the corpcard. TravelHub invoice shows "Total due 930.00 EUR" but the corpcard posted a charge for $1,200.00 USD. TravelHub says they passed a $200 refund from the airline back to them and issued a net invoice in EUR. Concur shows the $1,200 USD charge on the card. How do we reconcile the agency invoice vs posted card charge? Also I paid a last-minute checked bag on my personal card ($60) because agent couldn't add it to the ticket. Can that be reimbursed?

ExpenseBot: FYI per travel expense policy: agency invoices must include gross/credit lines if refunds were applied. Refund memos, airline refund refs, and the original agency invoice + payment receipt are required for AP reconciliation. FX differences are treated as realized exchange gains/losses and AP will post them to finance. Personal incidental charges (bags) are reimbursable with manager approval when incurred for business reasons. See https://redwood.internal/expenses/travel-invoice-guidance :page_with_curl:

Maya Chen (Finance): Hi Samir. AP will need: (1) TravelHub invoice PDF, (2) TravelHub refund memo showing airline refund reference, (3) card transaction id and posted amount (screenshot from Concur), and (4) airline refund reference if available. If TravelHub only issues a net invoice in EUR, AP must document the refund flow. We'll open an AP ticket to chase the agency for full backup.

Samir Hassan: Uploaded TravelHub invoice and Concur screenshot to the expense entry (link in Concur). TravelHub refund memo attached to their email thread but it only lists "credit applied" without airline ref. Card last4: 4321. Transaction id: ch_3Jk7l9.

Ruth Walker (Manager): Manager note: I approve reimbursement of the $60 baggage fee — it was necessary for client deliverable. Samir, please attach the bag receipt and add this approval note to Concur so AP has audit trail.

Maya Chen (Finance): Thanks Ruth. Samir, I'll open AP-TICKET-2026-201 to chase TravelHub for the airline refund reference or a credit memo showing the original airline refund transaction id. If TravelHub cannot provide airline ref, AP will document the agency-level credit and wait for the actual refunded cash/credit to appear on the corpcard posting. The FX difference (USD vs EUR) will be posted to the travel P&L FX variance account.

Samir Hassan: Uploaded bag receipt and added Ruth's approval comment to Concur. TravelHub replied asking for our corpcard statement line and said refunds usually post back to the agency account then to the card within 7-10 business days.

Maya Chen (Finance): OK we'll monitor the card account. Action items: AP-TICKET-2026-201 (agency chase), CONCUR-EXP-3310 (Samir reimbursement). Expect update in 3-7 business days. If refund posts as a separate credit to the corpcard, AP will net it against the charge and reconcile; if it posts to agency and not to our card, AP will request settlement proof.

AP Team: Opened AP-TICKET-2026-201. Noted: possible FX variance. Asked TravelHub to provide airline credit ref and timestamp.

Samir Hassan: One more Q: should I convert the agency EUR invoice in Concur to USD at the posted card rate or leave as EUR? Concur auto-converted it but the numbers differ.

Maya Chen (Finance): Leave the Concur item with the original vendor currency attachment and the posted card charge as the source of truth. AP will use the card posting for cash reconciliation and record any FX gain/loss separately. You can keep the vendor invoice as EUR attachment for VAT purposes.

ExpenseBot: Reminder: retain all email threads and the agency refund memo for 7 years for audit.

Samir Hassan: Thanks all — will follow up if TravelHub sends the airline ref. :thumbsup:
